refuter_findings.evidence: This carrier has kind: example, but its body uses ## Statement, ## Facts & Assumptions, and ## Proof. SCHEMA.md, Item bodies, specifies: “Use ## Example and optional ## Verification for an example.” The required ## Example heading is absent and the argument uses the theorem-style section structure.

The dependency def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state.md defines dimensionless torus coordinates θ and length coordinates X=L0θ for L0>0; b_i are orthonormal components in the length-coordinate frame. Step 3.1 writes the magnetic form using dx^i∧dx^j and gives period (2π)^2 b_i without identifying x with X or fixing L0=1 m. In the declared θ convention the form and period carry a factor L0², so the displayed exact period is not licensed, although its nonzero conclusion still follows from L0>0.

The summary states a magnetic period of (2π)^2 b_i. The dependency def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state.md sets X=L0θ with L0>0 and defines b_i in the length-coordinate frame. The page does not specify x=X or L0=1 m; under the declared θ convention the period includes L0². The exact value stated in the summary is therefore not licensed, though nonvanishing is preserved.

Clause 3 says a sequence of uniformly causal curves parametrized by auxiliary Riemannian arclength has a subsequential limit. The cited dependency thm-gr-limit-curve-two-endpoints.md explicitly assumes endpoint convergence, α_k(0)→x and α_k(b_k)→z, before giving that conclusion. Those hypotheses are absent here; on a noncompact globally hyperbolic spacetime, such curves can escape to infinity, so a convergent subsequence is not guaranteed.
